product_backlog.title: Core To-Do List MVP Functionality
product_backlog.description: Core functionality required for the to-do list web application MVP across Sprint 1.

acceptance_criteria: Given the user is on the home page, When they enter a list name and click create, Then a new to-do list is created and displayed.
Given lists exist, When the user views the home page, Then they see all their lists.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can successfully create and view separate lists.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name and see all my lists so that I can organize my tasks into categories.
product_backlog.title: Create and View To-Do Lists
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name and see all my lists so that I can organize my tasks into categories.

product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can successfully add tasks to specific lists.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to add a task with a short text description to a list so that I can keep track of things I need to do.
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing to-do list, When the user adds a task with a short text description, Then the task appears within that list.
product_backlog.title: Add Tasks to a List
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to add a task with a short text description to a list so that I can keep track of things I need to do.

product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can toggle task completion status and see visual differentiation.
product_backlog.title: Mark Tasks Complete or Incomplete
acceptance_criteria: Given a task in a list, When the user clicks to mark it complete, Then the task is visually distinguished as complete.
Given a completed task, When the user clicks to mark it incomplete, Then the task returns to incomplete status.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to mark a task as complete or incomplete so that I can track my progress.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to mark a task as complete or incomplete so that I can track my progress.

product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to delete a task or an entire list so that I can keep my to-do application clean and remove items I no longer need.
acceptance_criteria: Given a task exists in a list, When the user clicks delete on the task, Then the task is removed from the list.
Given a list exists, When the user clicks delete on the list, Then the list and all its tasks are deleted.
product_backlog.title: Delete Tasks and Lists
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can successfully clean up tasks and lists.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to delete a task or an entire list so that I can keep my to-do application clean and remove items I no longer need.

This is the fixed input fed verbatim to the agent team as the product vision for
every automated team-performance evaluation run (see `RELEASE.md` "Team performance
evaluation" and `agents/scrum_team/scripts/run_eval.py`). It is intentionally small
enough to be fully deliverable within a 5-sprint, small-budget run, while still
requiring real design decisions (state persistence, list vs. item modeling,
basic UI) that differentiate a good team performance from a mediocre one.

## Product Vision

Build a simple to-do list web application. A single user should be able to:

1. Create a new to-do list with a name.
2. Add a task to a list, with a short text description.
3. Mark a task as complete or incomplete.
4. Delete a task.
5. Delete an entire list (and its tasks).
6. See all their lists and, within a list, all its tasks, with completed tasks
   visually distinguished from incomplete ones.

## Constraints (deliberately narrow, to keep this deliverable in 5 sprints)

- **Single user, no authentication.** Do not build login/accounts — out of scope.
- **No persistence requirement beyond the current session/process is assumed** unless
  the team's own design calls for it — persistence approach (in-memory, file, or a
  simple embedded DB) is a legitimate design decision for the team to make and
  justify, not a hidden requirement.
- **A working web UI is required** — the deliverable is something a person could
  open in a browser and actually use, not just a backend API with no way to
  interact with it.
- **No specific language/framework is mandated.** The team should choose something
  it can deliver completely and correctly within budget, and should say why.

## Explicitly out of scope (do not let these creep in)

- Multiple users, sharing, or permissions.
- Due dates, reminders, priorities, tags, or sub-tasks.
- Mobile app, offline support, or real-time sync.
- Any deployment/hosting beyond running locally.

## What "done" looks like after 5 sprints

A person can clone the repo, follow the README, run the app, and actually create a
list, add a few tasks, mark one complete, delete one, and delete a list — end to
end, without reading any code first.
